topics.topic: Define the complete marked_at timestamp contract: authority, event meaning, read point/count, representation, invariant, and tests
questions: Which authoritative time source supplies the fresh instant written to `marked_at`?
Which event in the mark operation does `marked_at` denote: request receipt, acquisition of the project lock, successful Portal-photo validation, or creation of the mark record?
In which representation must `marked_at` be stored and returned, including time zone awareness, UTC offset, precision and serialization form?
How many readings of the decided time source may one mark operation take, and which reading supplies `marked_at`?
What authority supplies `marked_at`, what event does the instant mean, and at what point in a successful first mark is it read?
In which representation is `marked_at` stored and returned: aware UTC, naive UTC, configured local time, or another form?
What formal invariant and Required tests item must state and demonstrate the decided source, meaning, representation and number of clock readings for a newly written mark timestamp?
What source supplies `marked_at`, what datetime representation is stored, at what point in a successful mark operation is it read, and how many readings may that operation take?

judgement.why: This is the same complete marked_at authority, sampling-point, read-count, representation, invariant and test question already decided by P1, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Publication-mark timestamp authority, sampling event, clock-read count, and datetime representation
quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
precedent.why: A7 identifies the clock authority, fixes the single sampling point and read count, and specifies the exact UTC-naive microsecond representation and serialization.

topics.topic: Decide whether regular-file validation occurs before changing an existing lock entry's mode
questions: For an existing entry, must the service verify that it is a regular file before changing its mode, or may it set the mode first and then refuse it as non-regular?
After opening an existing non-regular entry, is regular-file validation performed before attempting to change its mode, or is the mode changed first?

quotes:
It is opened for reading and writing,
   created when absent, without following a link, and given the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE` each time it is
   opened, whatever the umask; a failure to set that mode is refused like a lock file that cannot be
   opened. An entry at its address that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is refused like a
   lock file that cannot be opened.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates the opened entry as a regular file before changing its mode, while another changes the mode first and then refuses it; an administrator inspecting the malformed entry observes whether its metadata changed.
judgement.why: The passage requires both validation and mode setting but does not order them for an existing entry.

topics.topic: Require a test demonstrating INV-12 for concurrent mark calls within one process

quotes: - INV-12: concurrent calls for one project never produce two placements or two marks for one source.

- INV-12: concurrent placements of one source, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed` and leave one placement record and one stored image (`test_separate_processes_leave_one_placement`), and marks from separate processes with two `photo_id` values answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).
judgement.divergence: One implementation serializes concurrent marks within one process and leaves one mark, while another passes the stated separate-process mark cases but permits two same-process calls to write; the callers and later readers of the mark notice the difference.
judgement.why: The unrestricted invariant covers concurrent marks in one process, but its Required tests item expressly requires in-process coverage only for placements and says only separate-process coverage for marks.

topics.topic: Specify a locking primitive and descriptor discipline that excludes both intra-process and inter-process concurrency
questions: Which locking primitive and descriptor discipline must be used so that concurrent calls in the same process, as well as calls in separate processes, actually exclude one another?

quotes:
Deliveries and marks of one project run one at a time, across processes, under an operating
   system lock on one lock file of that project in the state folder.
- INV-12: concurrent calls for one project never produce two placements or two marks for one source.
judgement.why: Any locking primitive and descriptor discipline is acceptable if it satisfies the stated same-project serialization and INV-12; an implementation that lets sibling threads pass concurrently violates those requirements rather than representing an allowed choice.

topics.topic: Specify durable-state assertions for the mark-concurrency test

quotes: - INV-12: concurrent calls for one project never produce two placements or two marks for one source.

- INV-12: concurrent placements of one source, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed` and leave one placement record and one stored image (`test_separate_processes_leave_one_placement`), and marks from separate processes with two `photo_id` values answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).
judgement.divergence: One test demonstrates that exactly one durable mark remains and contains the photo_id whose call returned `marked`, while another checks only response statuses and permits a response-compatible overwrite; a later scan or repeated delivery observes the wrong surviving photo_id.
judgement.why: The Required tests item states durable-state assertions for concurrent placements but only response assertions for concurrent marks, so it does not say what durable mark state must be demonstrated.
